content: Aristotle (384–322 BCE) was an ancient Greek philosopher, polymath, and founder of the Peripatetic school—student of Plato and tutor to Alexander the Great—whose systematic works on logic, metaphysics, ethics, politics, biology, and aesthetics profoundly shaped Western thought.
